description: Ultra-Fast Fashion, microplastic pollution, and poor environmental labor practice rankings.

entries.reason: Ultra-fast fashion adding 6,000+ synthetic polyester items daily; high levels of hazardous chemicals (lead, phthalates) identified by Greenpeace.
Disposability-first ultra-cheap supply chain driving massive international air-freight carbon emissions with zero environmental transparency.
Shein sister brand utilizing the same opaque, hyper-polluting synthetic supply chain with zero circularity.
Relies heavily on non-biodegradable virgin polyester, elastane, and toxic dye effluent; settlement with US FTC over wage theft and deceptive review suppression.
Sunday Times investigation revealed Leicester factory sweatshop labor under minimum wage and hazardous, unchecked fabric dyeing effluent.
Promotes 99% discount disposable consumerism; products made overwhelmingly of non-recycled fossil-fuel derived synthetics.
Algorithms-driven rapid garment production model with zero third-party environmental audits or supply-chain transparency.
Extreme fast fashion with opaque manufacturing, no traceability on raw materials, and high synthetic microplastic shed.
Sold £1 bikinis exemplifying hyper-disposable fashion that breaks down into persistent microplastics in oceans.
History of toxic chemical usage in textiles, low supply chain transparency, and landfill saturation.
High-volume discount apparel model reliant on low-cost labor and virgin synthetics that resist circular recycling.
Shares Boohoo Group's supply chain issues, with high proportions of virgin acrylic, nylon, and polyurethane.
AI-driven fast fashion with rapid trend generation and absence of verifiable carbon or microplastic mitigation commitments.
Massive volume production despite corporate pledges; millions of returns incinerated or dumped in global South landfills.
Pioneer of modern fast-fashion production cycles producing over 450 million garments annually with significant carbon footprint.
